title: NFL DRAFT
summary: Five pre-draft positions built from current market prices, top mock consensus, and late trade chatter for Round 1 on April 23, 2026.
market_context: DraftKings-linked markets posted by ESPN, FOX, DraftKings Network, CBS and Lineups on April 22-23, 2026. Core prices used: Over 1.5 QBs Round 1 -130; Jeremiyah Love 4th pick -135; Omar Cooper Jr. under 23.5 -160; Carnell Tate under 7.5 -105; KC Concepcion under 24.5 -140.
consensus: Fernando Mendoza is effectively locked at 1. After that, mocks split but repeatedly tie Ty Simpson to a late Round 1 trade-up, place Love in the 3-4 range, push Cooper into the middle of Round 1, keep Tate live in the 5-8 band, and cluster Concepcion around the early 20s.
rumors: The sharpest late-cycle smoke is about teams trading into the back of Round 1 for Ty Simpson before pick 33. Arizona keeps surfacing in Simpson chatter. Love-to-Arizona has market heat, but Tennessee at 4 remains a clean functional landing spot. Receiver demand from the Jets, Browns, Commanders, Saints and Eagles compresses the Cooper/Concepcion windows.

picks.logic: This is the cleanest way to express Ty Simpson late-first equity without paying the worst Simpson-specific juice. Multiple books and analysts still have him tied to a 25-32 range outcome even though the top-24 price is shaded to the over.
picks.slop_factor: Pick 33 is the fulcrum. Teams that want the fifth-year option have to jump the Jets at the top of Day 2, which creates real trade-up pressure at the end of Round 1.
picks.risk: If teams decide the class is too thin behind Mendoza and wait until Day 2, the board can die at one quarterback.

picks.prop: Jeremiyah Love to be drafted 4th overall
picks.logic: Love is live in the top four and Tennessee at 4 is the cleanest fit if Arizona either trades down or prioritizes trench value. The Titans can justify the draft capital by adding a true offensive multiplier to support Cam Ward.
picks.slop_factor: Public attention is concentrated on Love-to-Arizona at 3, which can hide the more stable structural case for Tennessee at 4.
picks.risk: Arizona could simply take him at 3, or a defensive player could push Love down one more slot.

picks.logic: Receiver demand in the middle of the round is strong, and Cooper's inside-outside flexibility plus run-after-catch profile make him a clean complement piece for several teams before pick 24.
picks.slop_factor: He is still discussed publicly like a second-wave receiver, but league-facing mocks keep placing him much closer to the middle of Round 1 because he gives coordinators instant YAC utility.
picks.risk: If teams in the 16-23 band pivot to trench players or corners, Cooper can get squeezed into the late first.

picks.logic: Tate remains the safest WR1 archetype in the class. The Browns, Commanders and Saints all have plausible pathways to taking a polished outside receiver in the 6-8 window.
picks.slop_factor: Jordyn Tyson steam has moved the conversation toward upside and medical recovery, which has created a cheaper number on the higher-floor receiver profile.
picks.risk: If Cleveland goes offensive line and Washington or New Orleans prefer another receiver archetype, Tate can slide beyond 8.

picks.logic: Concepcion's separation skill is the thing offensive staffs will pay for. His route suddenness and immediate slot/Z usability fit the early-20s zone better than the market suggests.
picks.slop_factor: The public still reads him as gadget-adjacent, but evaluators increasingly frame him as a first-round separator, which matters more than raw body type in this range.
picks.risk: If teams in the 20-24 band prioritize edge, line, or safety, he can fall into the late first or early second.
